skill.name: chipsec
skill.description: Analyze UEFI and BIOS firmware dumps offline with CHIPSEC. Inventory EFI modules, compare baselines, decode structures, inspect NVRAM, and scan for known threat signatures.
skill.summary: Guide offline CHIPSEC workflows for firmware threat scanning, inventory, decoding, NVRAM extraction, and baseline comparison.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, defensive malware terminology, and documented offline diagnostic commands. Six findings are confirmed in duplicated setup guidance that invokes sudo on a derived path and makes CHIPSEC log directories world-writable. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malware-enabling behavior was found.

remediation.issue: The setup applies mode 777 to the CHIPSEC logs directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use a user-owned log directory with the minimum required permissions, such as mode 0750, and never make package directories world-writable.

remediation.issue: Privileged commands use a path derived from system and user-controlled package locations.
remediation.suggestion: Reject empty results and require a verified, root-owned system installation path before any privileged filesystem operation.

remediation.issue: The stated rootless workflow includes duplicated sudo setup instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Document a rootless logging configuration and remove the sudo workaround from both setup and troubleshooting sections.

content.value_statement: Firmware dumps are difficult to inspect consistently, and missed changes can hide persistent threats. This skill provides repeatable offline CHIPSEC workflows for scanning, inventory, decoding, and comparison.
actual_capabilities: Provides CHIPSEC blocklist scan commands for supplied firmware images.
Generates EFI module inventories with GUIDs and cryptographic hashes.
Compares firmware images against known-good inventory baselines.
Decodes firmware volumes, EFI files, and available NVRAM data.
Parses SPI flash descriptors when the platform code is known.
Explains CHIPSEC exit codes, result states, and common troubleshooting steps.
limitations: Requires a local CHIPSEC installation and access to authorized firmware images.
Performs offline static analysis and cannot assess live hardware protections or runtime behavior.
Known-signature scans can miss new threats and require manual validation of matches.
Third-party parsers process untrusted firmware, so analysis should run in an isolated environment.

use_cases.title: Triage a firmware dump
use_cases.description: Scan an authorized image for known blocked EFI modules and summarize evidence for further investigation.

use_cases.title: Compare incident evidence
use_cases.description: Build inventories from suspect and known-good images, then identify changed EFI modules and hashes.

use_cases.title: Document device firmware
use_cases.description: Decode firmware structure, inventory modules, and extract available NVRAM information for an embedded device assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic threat scan
prompt_templates.prompt: I am authorized to analyze [firmware path]. Verify its format, run the offline CHIPSEC blocked-image scan, and summarize matches, errors, and next steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage of one firmware image

prompt_templates.title: Create a firmware inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an EFI inventory for [firmware path]. Report module names, GUIDs, hashes, inventory location, and any parsing failures without modifying the source image.

prompt_templates.title: Compare an update with a baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [updated firmware] against [baseline inventory]. Group added, removed, and changed EFI modules, then flag differences that need manual security review.

prompt_templates.title: Conduct a complete offline assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [firmware path] using threat scanning, EFI inventory, structure decoding, and NVRAM extraction. Include SPI descriptor analysis only when [platform code] is valid. Preserve evidence, record tool errors, and separate confirmed findings from uncertain indicators.

output_examples.input: Assess firmware.bin for known UEFI threats.
output: Format check: the image appears suitable for CHIPSEC offline parsing.
Threat scan: no blocked EFI signature match was reported.
Assessment: this result does not exclude unknown threats; create an inventory and review parser warnings.

output_examples.input: Compare firmware_updated.bin with the approved baseline.
output: Comparison summary: two EFI modules changed and one module was added.
Evidence: record each affected GUID and old and new hashes in the case notes.
Next step: validate the changes against the vendor update manifest before approval.

output_examples.input: Decode the firmware and inspect available NVRAM data.
output: Decode summary: firmware volumes and EFI sections were extracted to a separate analysis directory.
NVRAM summary: variable listings were present, but sensitive values require controlled handling.
Caution: preserve the original image and review all parser errors before drawing conclusions.

best_practices: Analyze only firmware you own or have explicit authorization to inspect.
Preserve the original image, record its hash, and perform parsing in an isolated workspace.
Validate every input and output path, and use user-owned directories with restrictive permissions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a passed signature scan as proof that firmware is clean.
Do not use sudo or world-writable package directories to solve logging errors.
Do not run live-driver commands when the task requires offline static analysis.

faq.question: Which firmware formats are supported?
faq.answer: The guide covers common UEFI images, including BIN, ROM, FD, CAP, SCAP, FV, and full flash dumps.

faq.question: Does offline analysis require root access?
faq.answer: Core offline commands use no kernel driver and should not require root. Configure a writable user-owned log directory instead of using sudo.

faq.question: Does the workflow modify the firmware image?
faq.answer: The documented scans read the source image. Decode and inventory operations create separate output files and directories.

faq.question: Can CHIPSEC detect every firmware threat?
faq.answer: No. Signature scans detect known patterns, while unknown implants and vendor-specific changes require deeper manual analysis.

faq.question: What does a failed or warning result mean?
faq.answer: A warning needs investigation. A failed result needs evidence review and remediation, while parser errors may indicate an unsupported format.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the authorized firmware path, analysis goal, known-good baseline when available, and platform code when SPI descriptor parsing is required.
